bug_description.normalized: A one-byte OpenPGP packet header (`0xAF`) is parsed as an indeterminate-length plaintext packet. `parse_plaintext()` allocates a `PKT_plaintext`, but `proc_plaintext()` frees the packet with `free_packet(pkt, NULL)` and then immediately reuses the dangling `pt` alias while constructing a `CTRLPKT_PLAINTEXT_MARK`, producing the observed heap-use-after-free read at `pt->namelen`.

source.description: This is the first project-side read of attacker input: `parse()` loads the witness byte into `ctb`, creating the raw packet-tag state that the header decoder immediately turns into the vulnerable plaintext path.
source.value_from: The staged witness file `poc` is exactly 1 byte long and contains `0xAF`. This read pulls that byte into `ctb`; the subsequent old-format decode derives `pkttype == PKT_PLAINTEXT`, `lenbytes == 0`, and `partial == 1` from the same value.
source.note: The external reproducer data first enters GnuPG here as the OpenPGP packet tag byte; the next decode step decides that it is an indeterminate-length plaintext packet.

tainted_value_origin.description: The sole attacker-controlled byte enters project state as `ctb = 0xAF`; the old-format header decode uses this value to select `PKT_PLAINTEXT` with indeterminate length, which is why the 1-byte file reaches the free-before-use path.

root_cause.description: The handler frees `pkt->pkt.plaintext` while the local alias `pt` is still live, so every later read of `pt->namelen`, `pt->mode`, `pt->name`, or `pt->timestamp` becomes a use-after-free.
root_cause.note: The patch fixes the bug by moving `free_packet (pkt, NULL);` and `c->last_was_session_key = 0;` below the `extrahash` construction.

sink.description: ASAN crash site. `proc_plaintext()` sizes `extrahash` by reading `pt->namelen` from the already-freed `PKT_plaintext` object.
sink.note: The sanitizer reports the heap-use-after-free READ at this statement; the read happens after `free_packet()` has already released the aliased `PKT_plaintext` object.

parser_admitted.code: rc = parse_plaintext (inp, pkttype, pktlen, pkt, new_ctb, partial);
parser_admitted.description: Once the header byte has been classified as `PKT_PLAINTEXT`, the packet parser enters `parse_plaintext()` on the witness input.

coarse_trace.summary: The 1-byte witness `0xAF` is read as the packet tag and decoded as an old-format indeterminate-length plaintext packet, selecting `parse_plaintext()`.
The plaintext parser allocates a `PKT_plaintext` object and materializes `mode`, `namelen`, and `timestamp` from the empty remainder of the stream.
The plaintext handler aliases that object as `pt`, then frees the packet before it is done using the alias.
Immediately after the free, the handler reads `pt->namelen` from the freed object to size `extrahash`, triggering the observed heap-use-after-free.

fine_trace.note: `parse()` consumes the only byte in the staged witness here. Because `poc` is exactly one byte long, this read loads `ctb = 0xAF` as the packet tag.

In the old-format decode block reached for `ctb = 0xAF`, bits 2-5 set `pkttype == PKT_PLAINTEXT`; because `(ctb & 3) == 3`, `lenbytes == 0`, so `pktlen` stays 0 and `partial` becomes 1 for an indeterminate-length plaintext packet.

fine_trace.var: mode, namelen, pkt->pkt.plaintext, pt->mode, pt->namelen, pt->timestamp
fine_trace.note: With no bytes left after the header, `iobuf_get_noeof()` yields `0xff` for both `mode` and `namelen`. `parse_plaintext()` allocates `pkt->pkt.plaintext` sized from that `namelen`, stores `pt->mode = 0xff` and `pt->namelen = 0xff`, zero-fills the absent filename bytes, and reads `pt->timestamp = 0xffffffff`.
When packet processing dispatches this plaintext packet to `proc_plaintext()`, the handler keeps `pt` as a local alias to the same heap object stored in `pkt->pkt.plaintext`.
`free_packet()` releases `pkt->pkt.plaintext`; for `PKT_PLAINTEXT`, that path reaches `free_plaintext()` and then `xfree(pt)`, so the still-live local alias `pt` now points at freed heap memory.

Immediately after the free, `proc_plaintext()` evaluates `6 + pt->namelen` to size `extrahash`, re-reading `pt->namelen` through the dangling alias. ASAN reports the 4-byte heap-use-after-free READ at this line.

poc.trigger: The staged witness file `poc` is the exact saved external reproducer: a 1-byte file containing `0xAF`, which libFuzzer runs as `/tmp/poc`. In `_work/src/fuzz_verify.c:125-135`, the harness truncates `/tmp/fuzzdirverify/fuzz.gpg`, writes that byte sequence into the temp file, then calls `verify_signatures()` on it and reaches the ASAN heap-use-after-free in `proc_plaintext()` at `g10/mainproc.c:956`.

format.name: single-byte old-format OpenPGP plaintext-packet header
format.contract: A one-byte file whose sole byte is `0xAF`, i.e. an old-format packet tag with packet type 11 (`PKT_PLAINTEXT`) and indeterminate length. No trailing bytes are required for the witnessed crash path.
